lines.trans: Vika, look at me. What is this?
Chef, this is my new little dog!
I bought her this morning.
Why do you need a dog of the same breed?
I just really liked your Dyson.
I could not resist and bought a puppy.
But they are completely identical!
Sorry, I still mix them up.
It seems this one is yours, and this one is mine.
Vika, what is your dog's name?
Mine? His name is Maxik!
And what breed is this dog?
Breed sushi... Oh, Shih Tzu!
Just like your dog. I will go!

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: person who likes is in the dative

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.
Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: звать на помощь = to call for help
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
instrumental of утро used as an adverb

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: grammatically feminine even for a male dog
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: used in 'до сих пор' = until now, up to this point

examples.text: Я до сих пор ничего не понял.

examples.trans: Right away. Everything will be ready.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рода'). Common feminine noun meaning 'breed' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Подскажите, пожалуйста, какая у него порода?
examples.trans: Could you tell me, please, what breed he is?
What is this breed called, Shih Tzu?
Can I go and have a look?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Grab the little dog in the park and run.
What a funny little white dog!
The little dog is small and friendly.

examples.text: Да все вы одинаковые! Разговор окончен, идите!
examples.trans: You're all the same! The conversation is over, leave!

examples.text: Я не удержалась и купила пёсика.
examples.trans: I could not resist and bought a puppy.
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
All right, here you go. There, look.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

examples.text: Тут есть пицца, суши и борщ.
examples.trans: They have pizza, sushi, and borscht here.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Извините, я их до сих пор путаю.
examples.trans: Sorry, I still mix them up.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Я не удержалась и купила пёсика.
examples.trans: I could not resist and bought a puppy.

examples.text: Это слово «удержаться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to resist' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dog, hound' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To give boots to vicious dogs.

examples.text: Сначала мы отдадим твои сапоги злым псам.
examples.trans: First we will give your boots to the vicious dogs.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
